description: CGV-2 Memory management: list with trust+category filters, add/edit form, one-tap verify, delete with confirm, and a guarded conflict-resolve affordance. Backend memories module is a STUB (404 until MEM-2/MEM-4), so build the full UI/forms/nav/validation wired to the documented contract and note the stub in code + verification. Depends on FEAT-001 (PIN gate + nav shell). Independent of FEATs 003-005.
steps: Read context.json and this FEAT file FIRST.

Rebuild app/(caregiver)/memories/index.tsx: list via listMemories(filter) from src/api/memories. Each row shows the shared TrustBadge (from FEAT-001) + the memory category + a short content preview. Add filter controls for trust (Trust union) and category (Category union) that re-call listMemories with a MemoryFilter {trust?, category?}. Provide one-tap Verify per row -> verifyMemory(id) then refresh. Provide Delete per row with a confirm Alert -> deleteMemory(id).

Add a new form route app/(caregiver)/memories/[id].tsx (use id==='new' for create, an existing id for edit; read the id via useLocalSearchParams). Fields: content (required, multiline), category (segmented over Category), importance (segmented over Importance), validity (segmented over Validity), and valid_from/valid_until shown ONLY when validity is 'scheduled' or 'temporary' (plain TextInput with YYYY-MM-DD hint). Optional person via a picker populated from listPeople() (src/api/people) rendering names (reuse PersonCard or a simple row). Create via createMemory(input: MemoryInput), edit via updateMemory(id, input). Navigate here from the list's Add/Edit buttons with router.push.

Add a conflict-resolve affordance for rows whose trust is 'conflicting': resolve keeps one memory verified (verifyMemory) and archives the other (updateMemory(otherId, { validity: 'archived' })) following the documented resolution path. GUARD it: if any resolve call throws an ApiError with status 404, show a 'conflict resolution available once the memories module lands (MEM-4)' message instead of crashing.
Implement loading/error (catch instanceof ApiError, show err.message + retry)/empty states on both the list and the form.
Add an inline code comment that the memories backend is a stub (routes 404 until MEM-2/MEM-4) and the screen is wired to the documented contract.
acceptance_criteria: The list shows each memory's trust via TrustBadge and can filter by trust and by category.
Verify is one tap from the list and calls verifyMemory.
The add/edit form sets content, category, importance, validity, validity dates (only for scheduled/temporary), and an optional person, calling createMemory/updateMemory with MemoryInput.
Delete asks for confirmation and calls deleteMemory.
The conflict-resolve affordance is wired to verifyMemory + updateMemory(archived) and is guarded against a 404 from the stubbed backend.
From mobile/: npx tsc --noEmit prints zero errors and grep -rn 'fetch(' app returns nothing.
findings:
DELIVERED: app/(caregiver)/memories/index.tsx (rebuilt list) and app/(caregiver)/memories/[id].tsx (new add/edit form). Registered <Stack.Screen name="memories/[id]"/> in app/(caregiver)/_layout.tsx right after memories/index (matching FEAT-001's nav-shell contract). Build gate GREEN: npx tsc --noEmit exits 0 with zero errors; grep -rn 'fetch(' app returns nothing.

LIST (memories/index.tsx): listMemories(filter) via src/api/memories. Each row = TrustBadge (import `../../../src/components/TrustBadge`, props {trust, theme}) + category label + 3-line content/title preview. Two FilterChips rows (trust union + category union); tapping a chip sets MemoryFilter and re-calls listMemories, tapping the active chip or 'All' clears it. Per-row actions: Edit -> router.push({pathname:'/(caregiver)/memories/[id]', params:{id}}); Verify (hidden when already verified) -> verifyMemory(id) then refresh; Delete -> Alert.alert confirm -> deleteMemory(id). Conflict rows (trust==='conflicting') get an extra 'Resolve conflict' button -> verifyMemory(this) + updateMemory(conflicts_with, {validity:'archived'}), GUARDED: ApiError status===404 shows 'available once the memories module lands (MEM-4)' instead of crashing. Reload driven by useFocusEffect so returning from the form refreshes. Three states: loading (ActivityIndicator), error (ApiError.message + Try again), empty (filter-aware message). Per-row busyId prevents one action from locking the whole list.

FORM (memories/[id].tsx): id==='new' => createMemory, else getMemory(id) prefill + updateMemory(id). id read via useLocalSearchParams<{id:string}>(). Fields: content (required multiline; validated non-empty before save), category/importance/validity segmented single-selects over the exact src/types unions, valid_from/valid_until (YYYY-MM-DD TextInputs) rendered ONLY when validity is 'scheduled' or 'temporary' and sent as null otherwise, optional person via listPeople() rendered with reused PersonCard (hubUrl from getHubUrl()); 'No one' row clears it. Payload typed as MemoryInput. People load is tolerant (listPeople stub failure -> empty list, form still usable). Three states: loading/error(retry+back)/empty-people note.

STUB NOTE: memories (and people) routes 404 until MEM-2/MEM-4; both screens are wired to the documented contract and surface ApiError.message in their error state. No raw fetch anywhere — all I/O through src/api/*. Reused BigButton + PersonCard + TrustBadge; added no new shared components (segmented/chip controls are local to these screens).

FOLLOW-UP for FEAT-001 dashboard: now that memories/[id] exists, memory/flagged rows could be re-pointed from router.push('/(caregiver)/memories') to router.push({pathname:'/(caregiver)/memories/[id]', params:{id}}) if deep-edit is wanted — not required by FEAT-002, left as-is.
